proposed_record.reviewerRationale: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation is recommended for green private review as a Canadian space and defence developer with unusually broad, independently corroborated work across strategic micro-nuclear power, lunar water purification, lunar resource processing, portable multi-sensor imaging and quantum subsurface sensing. Federal sources confirm the former-name continuity, incorporation in 2020, current Waterloo activity, multiple CSA programs, a National Defence IDEaS project and a $4.5 million FedDev contribution. The reviewer should preserve the development-stage labels, verify the preferred Waterloo-versus-Toronto primary location, and treat the Luxembourg QASM relationship as company-reported until an agency source is available.
reviewWarnings: LEUNR is development-stage. Government evidence supports funded prototype work, while the 2029 demonstration target is a company projection rather than proof of licensing or deployment.
QASM technical and contract details are sourced to a company-issued announcement; no independent Luxembourg Space Agency project page was resolved.

The latest FedDev profile calls CSMC Waterloo-based, while CSA and other official records retain Toronto locations. Waterloo is proposed as the city-centroid map location pending reviewer confirmation.
CSMC Nuclear and CSMC Labs are described by the company as wholly owned, but their separate legal registrations were not independently resolved in this run.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: The federal trademark record documents the formal transition from Canadian Space Mining Corporation to Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation and a technology scope spanning nuclear, quantum, aerospace and geophysical work.

The newest federal economic-development profile describes CSMC as Waterloo-based; a Waterloo city-centroid location is used while the Toronto-versus-Waterloo headquarters question remains visible for review.

CSMC's official site describes wholly owned nuclear and R&D divisions working across microreactors, quantum, robotics, nanomaterials, electrochemistry, industrial automation, natural resources and space systems.
FedDev Ontario records an active $10.095 million micro-nuclear development project supported by a $4.5 million federal contribution for Arctic defence and remote-energy applications.
The official website provides a public contact form with routes for partnerships, investors, media, careers and general inquiries.
CSMC describes LEUNR as an adaptation of Canadian research-reactor technology for portable remote and commercial power, with a company target to demonstrate the system by 2029.
The Canadian Space Agency funds a non-fuel prototype test intended to confirm performance and advance the Low Enriched Uranium Nuclear Reactor toward mission readiness.
The Canadian Space Agency identifies LunaPure as the Aqualunar grand-prize-winning, self-contained and low-maintenance system for purifying water from lunar polar regions.
The Canadian Space Agency describes HYDRO+ as an integrated gas-reduction prototype for processing diverse ore and minerals from different lunar geological regions.
The NRC IRAP record describes a low-power, inexpensive and man-portable multi-sensor imaging concept with geotechnical, medical-tomography and advanced-manufacturing inspection applications.
CSMC's attributed announcement describes QASM as a space-based quantum-gravimetry sensor for detecting and characterizing subsurface critical minerals and water from Earth or planetary orbit.
FedDev Ontario records a $4.5 million contribution toward a $10.095 million project to advance CSMC micro-nuclear technology for Arctic defence and remote energy.
National Defence records a $1 million LEUNR project under the IDEaS NORAD Modernization Science and Technology Contest through September 2027.
The Canadian Space Agency records a $1 million advanced-technology contribution for the LEUNR non-fuel prototype and space micro modular reactor development.
The Canadian Space Agency selected CSMC as the Stage 3 Aqualunar winner and awarded $400,000 to continue LunaPure development.
The Canadian Space Agency awarded $499,647 to advance the HYDRO+ lunar resource-processing prototype.
CSMC is one of three Canadian companies receiving four CSA contracts totalling $2 million for ten-month lunar regolith-management and surface-power architecture studies.
NRC IRAP records a $75,000 contribution to validate CSMC's Time and Impedance Multi-Sensor concept.
CSMC reports a Luxembourg Space Agency contract for the QASM space-based quantum-sensing system.
Canadian Space Agency sources document CSMC across current architecture studies and earlier funded LEUNR, LunaPure and HYDRO+ work.
National Defence and DRDC support CSMC's LEUNR work through the IDEaS NORAD-modernization research program.
FedDev Ontario provides a $4.5 million contribution toward CSMC's current micro-nuclear technology scale-up project.
CSMC reports that the Luxembourg Space Agency awarded the company a contract to develop QASM for quantum resource sensing.
The official site identifies CSMC Nuclear as a wholly owned subsidiary focused on portable nuclear reactors for remote environments.
The official site identifies CSMC Labs as a wholly owned R&D division commercializing deep technologies in quantum, natural resources and related fields.

organization.name: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation
organization.description: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation is a Waterloo-based Canadian space and defence technology company developing dual-use systems for strategic power, remote and Arctic operations, space resources, water purification and advanced sensing.

profileData.foundedAndIdentity: Incorporated in 2020 as Canadian Space Mining Corporation and renamed Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation in December 2025, with the federal name record registered in January 2026.
profileData.operatingModel: CSMC presents CSMC Nuclear as its wholly owned strategic-power subsidiary and CSMC Labs as its wholly owned R&D division for quantum, natural resources and other deep technologies.
profileData.canadianFootprint: FedDev Ontario describes the company as Waterloo-based in July 2026. Canadian Space Agency and other federal records also identify Toronto activity under the current and former names.
profileData.portfolioScope: Development-stage micro-nuclear reactors; lunar water purification and resource processing; portable multi-sensor imaging; quantum-gravimetry sensing; and broader R&D in robotics, nanomaterials, electrochemistry, industrial automation and space systems.
profileData.currentActivity: Current public activity includes a $10.095 million FedDev-supported microreactor project, National Defence and CSA LEUNR projects, the Aqualunar-winning LunaPure system, lunar architecture studies and a company-reported Luxembourg QASM contract.
profileData.publicContact: CSMC provides a public web form for partnerships, investors, media, careers and general inquiries at https://strategicmissions.ca/.
profileData.evidenceBoundary: Technology descriptions, awards and programs are source-backed. Maturity labels are preserved, and mission matches are derived analyst assessments rather than procurement eligibility, endorsement, customer interest or classified demand.

capabilities.name: LEUNR Micro-Nuclear Reactor
capabilities.summary: Develop a portable low-enriched-uranium microreactor derived from Canadian research-reactor technology to provide resilient power for remote, Arctic, defence and space applications; current work remains at funded prototype and demonstration-planning stage.
capabilities.capabilityType: Development-stage portable micro modular nuclear reactor

missionMatches.alignmentSummary: If successfully demonstrated and deployed, LEUNR could provide persistent power for remote sensors, communications and edge-computing infrastructure where conventional logistics are constrained.

LEUNR's stated Arctic and remote-power posture could enable sustained operation of northern sensing and communications sites, although the reactor itself is an enabling power system rather than an awareness sensor.

capabilities.name: LunaPure Lunar Water Purification
capabilities.summary: Purify water extracted from lunar polar regions through a self-contained, low-maintenance and sustainable system intended to support long-duration human and robotic exploration while informing terrestrial water-treatment innovation.

capabilities.name: HYDRO+ Lunar Resource Processing
capabilities.summary: Process diverse lunar ores and minerals using an integrated gas-reduction approach designed for different geological regions and future in-situ resource-utilization operations on the Moon.
features: Adaptation to different lunar geological regions
Prototype funded by the Canadian Space Agency

capabilities.name: Time and Impedance Multi-Sensor Imaging
capabilities.summary: Provide a low-power, inexpensive and man-portable multi-sensor imaging concept for subsurface and volumetric characterization across critical-mineral exploration, field medical imaging and advanced-manufacturing inspection.

capabilities.name: QASM Quantum Atomic Subsurface Mapper
capabilities.summary: Detect and characterize subsurface critical minerals and water using a proposed space-based quantum-gravimetry sensor designed for observation from Earth orbit and other planetary bodies.

missionMatches.alignmentSummary: A mature orbital quantum-gravimetry system could contribute a distinct geophysical layer for remote northern terrain and resource characterization; this is a derived potential because QASM remains development-stage.

programs.summary: A $499,647 Canadian Space Agency project to prototype CSMC's integrated gas-reduction HYDRO+ system for processing lunar ores and minerals.

programs.summary: CSMC participates in ten-month Canadian Space Agency architecture studies assessing lunar regolith management and surface power; four contracts totalling $2 million were awarded across three Canadian companies.

programs.summary: A $75,000 NRC IRAP project to validate the Time and Impedance Multi-Sensor imaging concept for resource exploration, medical tomography and manufacturing inspection.
